title: Rotary Torso Machine
summary: A seated machine that rotates your torso against resistance, for direct oblique work.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for obliques (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly obliques total.
Library rating 0.3 for abs (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly abs total.

setup.text: Sit with your knees locked in and your chest against the pads.
Rotate your torso to one side through a comfortable range.
Return slowly, then do the other side.

form_cues.cue: Rotate the torso to one side
Move slowly. Don't let the weight swing you back.

mistakes.text: Using momentum to swing the pad.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stable, One side at a time, More systemic fatigue.
Swap sheet: Better isolation, Lower loading potential, Steadier cable tension.
Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Better isolation, Less stable.
